cues.zh: 然后我参与这个项目，我飞来飞去，我是星空联盟金卡会员，能享受一些不错的小福利，我觉得这些挺重要的。

cues.en: So identity is also
cues.zh: 所以身份也是

cues.en: what I like.
cues.zh: 我喜欢的东西。

cues.en: I like the Canucks. I like the Grizzlies, at least until they got sold.
cues.zh: 我喜欢Canucks队。我喜欢Grizzlies队，至少在他们被卖掉之前。

cues.en: These are books that have influenced me.
cues.zh: 这些是影响过我的书。

cues.zh: 我关注这些杂志来了解动态，

cues.en: and movies that I relate to. And obviously, I like Apple equipment. This is what I like to wear. This is what I like to drive.
cues.zh: 还有我产生共鸣的电影。显然，我喜欢Apple的设备。这是我喜欢的穿着。这是我喜欢的车。

cues.en: So that's me. That's part of my identity.
cues.zh: 这就是我。这是我身份的一部分。

cues.en: So how is it conveyed? Well, historically, it's been verbal where you trusted the person you're talking to, and then we had things like patents and ability, but anyone saw a knight's tale and knows that those could be forged.
cues.zh: 那它怎么传递呢？历史上，靠的是口头表达，你信任跟你说话的人，后来有了专利和能力证明之类的东西，但看过《圣战骑士》的人都知道，那些是可以伪造的。

cues.en: And, you know, so we had official papers which enabled trust on a local scale, but modern identity has really been around photo ID, where we had passports and driver's license and student cards that enabled trust on a global scale that I could prove that I was Canadian, that I live here, and that I went to UBC, and that I'm over 21.
cues.zh: 所以，我们有了官方文件，能在本地范围内建立信任，但现代身份主要还是围绕带照片的证件，我们有护照、驾照和学生卡，能在全球范围内建立信任，让我能证明我是加拿大人、我住在这里、我上过UBC、我超过21岁。

cues.en: You know, so identity is what I say about me,
cues.zh: 你知道，身份就是我怎么描述自己，

cues.en: what others say about me.
cues.zh: 以及别人怎么描述我。

cues.en: Of course, what others say is more trusted.
cues.zh: 当然，别人说的更可信。

cues.en: You know, identity is really reputation. You know, it's what others say about you. So where is identity used? Well, we have all kinds of identity transactions.
cues.zh: 你知道，身份其实就是声誉。就是别人怎么描述你。那么身份用在哪些地方呢？我们有各种各样的身份事务。

cues.en: Some of those are verbal. You meet somebody, you say your name, you say where you work. You may even do the same thing over the telephone or other things like a job application where you fill in a form,
cues.zh: 有些是口头的。你遇到某人，说出你的名字，说你在哪工作。你可能在电话里也做同样的事，或者像求职申请那样填表格，

cues.en: and all this stuff is unverified. You really need to trust the person you're dealing with. But what about verified
cues.zh: 而这些东西都是未经核实的。你真的需要信任和你打交道的人。但经过核实的

cues.en: identity? Well, a familiar example is when you go to a place like this, and of course you to be over 21 and you walk up to the cashier and they say, you know, some ID.
cues.zh: 身份呢？一个熟悉的例子是，你去像这样的地方，当然你得年满21岁，你走到收银员面前，他们说，出示一下身份证。

cues.en: You then have a choice, of course, as to whether or not you even want to present ID. Of course, you don't get to buy your booth if you don't do that. You can decide which ID to show, which is another important aspect. You can show your passport, you can show your driver's license, some places even take your student card.
cues.zh: 然后你当然可以选择是否要出示身份证。当然，不出示就买不到酒。你可以决定出示哪种身份证，这是另一个重要方面。你可以出示护照，可以出示驾照，有些地方甚至接受学生证。

cues.en: So, me, I'll go and show my driver's license, and they'll go and compare the photos on there, and they'll see that the subject actually does match a credential.
cues.zh: 所以，我呢，我会去出示我的驾照，他们会比对上面的照片，看看本人确实和证件匹配。

cues.en: And a nice feature of this is, of course, that only I can go and use my driver's license. And then they look at that and they see, okay, well who issued it? Does it look like it's authentic?
cues.zh: 这的一个好处当然是，只有我才能使用我的驾照。然后他们看了之后，看看，好，是谁签发的？看起来像真的吗？

cues.en: Is it still valid? And through that they see it's a valid credential, assuming they trust the province of BC.
cues.zh: 它还有效吗？通过这种方式，他们看到这是一个有效凭证，前提是他们信任BC省。

cues.en: And then
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: they look at it and they need to figure out the age, and so they look to see what
cues.zh: 他们查看它，需要弄清楚年龄，于是他们去看

cues.en: those parts are, and they see that, well yeah, he is definitely over 21, so he's authorized to go and get his Vanilla Stoli.
cues.zh: 那些部分是什么，然后他们看到，嗯是的，他肯定超过21岁了，所以他有资格去买他的Vanilla Stoli。

cues.en: So, you know, things like this have dramatically reduced the friction in identity transactions.
cues.zh: 所以，你知道，这类事情极大地减少了身份交易中的摩擦。

cues.en: And photo ID,
cues.zh: 还有带照片的身份证件，

cues.en: interesting enough, is an asymmetry trust because there's no relationship between the province of BC and the cashier,
cues.zh: 有趣的是，这是一种不对称信任，因为BC省和收银员之间没有关系，

cues.en: which provides extreme scalability.
cues.zh: 这提供了极高的可扩展性。

cues.en: And a province is not a participant in identity transaction,
cues.zh: 而省份并不是身份交易的参与者，

cues.en: which provides a bunch of privacy features. They have no idea where and when I am showing that credential.
cues.zh: 这提供了许多隐私特性。他们完全不知道我在何时何地出示那个凭证。

cues.en: And the credential's also reusable by any recipient
cues.zh: 而且该凭证还可被任何接收方重复使用

cues.en: who trusts the issuer, in this case, of course, a province of BC. So to summarize, identity is what I say about me,
cues.zh: 只要他们信任签发方，在这个例子中，当然就是BC省。所以总结一下，身份就是我关于自己的陈述，

cues.en: it's what others say about me,
cues.zh: 是别人关于我的陈述，

cues.en: and modern identity is enabled to separation between the acquisition
cues.zh: 而现代身份实现了获取

cues.en: and the presentation of the credential, as well as identification process and the authorization process.
cues.zh: 和出示凭证之间的分离，以及身份识别过程和授权过程的分离。

cues.en: And it provides,
cues.zh: 它提供了，

cues.en: you know, extreme scale and a lot of privacy
cues.zh: 你知道，极大的规模和大量隐私

cues.en: that I control,
cues.zh: 由我控制，

cues.en: at least most of the time.
cues.zh: 至少大多数时候是这样。

cues.en: So what is digital identity?
cues.zh: 那么什么是数字身份？

cues.en: Well, we have site registration,
cues.zh: 嗯，我们有网站注册，

cues.en: we go and fill in often what is the same information
cues.zh: 我们经常去填写相同的信息

cues.en: at a whole bunch of different sites.
cues.zh: 在一大堆不同的网站上。

cues.en: And,
cues.zh: 还有，

cues.en: you know,
cues.zh: 你知道，

cues.en: that's obviously a bit of a hassle.
cues.zh: 这显然有点麻烦。

cues.en: It could be simpler.
cues.zh: 本可以更简单。

cues.en: You know, is a digital identity? Well, I think it is, but it's unverified and it's like verbal information where when you meet somebody except there's fewer trust cues because you can't see the person, you can't hear the person, in fact, might not even even be a person at the other end of the farm.
cues.zh: 你知道，数字身份是什么？嗯，我认为它是，但它未经核实，就像口头信息一样——当你见到某人时，只不过信任线索更少，因为你看不到对方，听不到对方，事实上，电话那头甚至可能根本不是人。

cues.en: So what about username and password or say your secure ID token? Well, I think of this as just authentication,
cues.zh: 那么用户名和密码，或者你的安全ID令牌呢？嗯，我认为这仅仅是身份验证，

cues.en: and it proves that you are a directory entry.
cues.zh: 它证明你是一个目录条目。

cues.en: I consider this identity one o. It's directory centric. It's an opaque trust decision. There's a single authority.
cues.zh: 我认为这是身份1.0。它以目录为中心。这是一个不透明的信任决策。只有一个权威机构。

cues.en: There's no credential choice. It's not portable. It's all in a silo. How do we mimic the real world? Where's my digital driver's license? How do I prove that I'm Canadian, that I'm... Live here, that I'm 21, I went to UBC, I'm at Skip, I'm the CEO there, and I'm Star Alliance Gold, you know, important thing online. How do I prove any of this stuff online? It's not possible. Today, verified digital identity is not anything that you can give to the site,
cues.zh: 没有凭证选择。不可移植。全都在一个孤岛里。我们如何模拟现实世界？我的数字驾照在哪里？我如何证明我是加拿大人，我……住在这里，我21岁，我上过UBC，我在Skip，我是那里的CEO，我是星空联盟金卡会员，你知道，这在网上很重要。我如何在网上证明这些？不可能。今天，经过验证的数字身份不是你能交给网站的任何东西，

cues.en: but it's what a website knows about you. So one of the best examples of that is your eBay reputation that you build up over time, but try and take that over to Craigslist. Is it your reputation or their reputation? It's closed. Or take all the books you bought at amazon.com over to Barnes and Noble so they can help you out. You can't do that. It's a walled garden. We have all these identity silos
cues.zh: 而是网站对你的了解。最好的例子之一就是你在eBay上随着时间建立起来的声誉，但试着把它带到Craigslist上。这是你的声誉还是他们的声誉？它是封闭的。或者把你在amazon.com上买的所有书带到Barnes and Noble，让他们帮你。你做不到。这是一个围墙花园。我们有所有这些身份孤岛

cues.en: and you can't move the identity around between them. It's site centric with a site in the middle. This is identity one point o. What we really want is something that's user centric, where the user's in the middle, and the user can move their identity from any site to any site.
cues.zh: 而且你无法在它们之间移动身份。它以网站为中心，网站居于中间。这就是身份1.0。我们真正想要的是以用户为中心的东西，用户居于中间，用户可以将他们的身份从任何网站移动到任何网站。

cues.en: And then that gives us Identity two point o. So why will Identity two point o happen?
cues.zh: 然后这就引出了 Identity 2.0。那么，Identity 2.0 为什么会发生呢？

cues.en: Well, in general, simple and open win.
cues.zh: 嗯，总的来说，简单和开放会胜出。

cues.en: We have client server got replaced by HTTP and HTML, lease lines and frame relay got replaced by the Internet because these things were silos, they were closed, they were complex.
cues.zh: 我们的客户端-服务器被 HTTP 和 HTML 取代，租用线路和帧中继被互联网取代，因为这些东西都是孤岛，它们是封闭的、复杂的。

cues.en: You had electronic mail systems like MCI Mail, CompuServe Mail, Props, X400,
cues.zh: 你曾经有像 MCI Mail、CompuServe Mail、Props、X400 这样的电子邮件系统，

cues.en: which were enterprise email solutions, but where are they today? They're gone. Something simple and open one, SMTP,
cues.zh: 它们是企业级电子邮件解决方案，但今天它们在哪里？它们已经消失了。某个简单而开放的东西胜出了，SMTP，

cues.en: which became ubiquitous and many considered the killer app of the Internet, which of course led to its own problems, but that's another story.
cues.zh: 它变得无处不在，许多人认为它是互联网的杀手级应用，这当然也导致了它自身的问题，但那是另一个故事了。

cues.en: So, simple and open wins. So today, you know, identity is in a silo. It's in walled gardens as close and complex.
cues.zh: 所以，简单和开放会胜出。那么今天，你知道，身份处于孤岛之中。它处于封闭而复杂的围墙花园里。

cues.en: Simple and open is inevitable, and being able to take your identity from any site to any site, and being able to have IdentityTO is bound to happen. So what does it look like? Well,
cues.zh: 简单和开放是不可避免的，能够把你的身份从任何站点带到任何站点，以及能够拥有 Identity 2.0，是必然会发生的。那么它是什么样子呢？嗯，

cues.en: in Identity one o, we have the user who goes to present some account credentials to a resource, and the resource goes and checks the directory and sees whether or the user's allowed in. So to do this, the directory needs identity of the resource. And of course, that means the more resources, the more management there is around that. It's a symmetrical trust relationship.
cues.zh: 在 Identity 1.0 中，我们有用户去向某个资源出示一些账户凭据，然后该资源去检查目录，看看用户是否被允许进入。所以要做到这一点，目录需要该资源的身份标识。当然，这意味着资源越多，围绕它的管理就越多。这是一种对称的信任关系。

cues.en: And the policy decision is opaque. If you think about it, sort of like if I went to the cashier, I told her my name,
cues.zh: 而策略决策是不透明的。你想想，就好比我去收银台，告诉收银员我的名字，

cues.en: and she phoned up the province of BC to decide whether or not I gotta buy my bottle of vanilla. That's kinda crazy.
cues.zh: 然后她打电话给BC省，来决定我能不能买这瓶香草精。这有点离谱。

cues.en: So in Identity 2.0, the user goes and there's a credential provider. They get their credentials,
cues.zh: 所以在Identity 2.0中，用户去找凭证提供方，拿到他们的凭证，

cues.en: and they go to a resource. Resource says what they want. They give that credential to the resource, sort of how it is in the real world.
cues.zh: 然后他们去访问某个资源。资源方说明需要什么。用户把凭证交给资源方，就像现实世界中的做法一样。

cues.en: And that I can go and take that same credential and provide it to different resources,
cues.zh: 而且我可以拿着同一份凭证，提供给不同的资源方，

cues.en: or that I can go and get credentials from
cues.zh: 或者我可以从

cues.en: a bunch of different providers and provide it the same resource, you can provide them all to the same resource. So you have transparent policy, it's much simpler, it scales, and it's flexible.
cues.zh: 多个不同的提供方获取凭证，再提供给同一个资源方，可以把它们全部交给同一个资源方。这样就实现了透明的策略，简单得多，可扩展，而且灵活。

cues.en: So who will drive this?
cues.zh: 那么谁来推动这件事呢？

cues.en: Now, what about the users? Well, they have too many usernames and passwords. They really love the idea. We did some user testing. Of course, they won't pay, and they have little influence. So, it's really unlikely.
cues.zh: 那用户呢？他们的用户名和密码太多了，他们真的很喜欢这个想法。我们做过一些用户测试。当然，他们不会付费，而且影响力也很小。所以，这不太可能。

cues.en: What
cues.zh: 那

cues.en: about the enterprise? They have a proliferation of partners, contractors, agents. They have a directory centric model that's crumbling, but
cues.zh: 企业呢？他们的合作伙伴、承包商、代理越来越多。他们那种以目录为中心的模式正在崩塌，但

cues.en: it's risky for them to lead anything like this. They have a lot of existing infrastructure. In many ways, they can't get there from here. The next logical step for them is federation,
cues.zh: 让他们来引领这种事是有风险的。他们有大量现有基础设施。从很多方面来说，他们没法从这里到达那里。对他们来说，下一个合乎逻辑的步骤是联邦化，

cues.en: what I call Identity 1.5.
cues.zh: 也就是我所说的Identity 1.5。

cues.en: So, it's unlikely they're going grab it. What about government?
cues.zh: 所以，他们不太可能抓住这个机会。那政府呢？

cues.en: Well, some of them are trying to go to e government. They have all these different departments. They have these identity silos, so maybe, but it's pretty localized. They have cross border jurisdictional issues. What about banks?
cues.zh: 嗯，有些政府正试图推行电子政务。他们设有各种不同的部门，存在身份信息孤岛，所以或许有可能，但相当本地化。他们还面临跨境管辖权问题。那银行呢？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: there's been a bunch of issues here around phishing and farming, so they're pretty motivated.
cues.zh: 这里存在一系列网络钓鱼和农场上欺诈的问题，所以他们很有动力。

cues.en: In theory, have a trust relationship with the user, so that's possible.
cues.zh: 理论上，与用户之间存在信任关系，所以这是可能的。

cues.en: What about the websites, big portals? Well, I mean, you need really a whole identity ecosystem. So you need lots of users. You need a bunch of identity providers and service providers that are loosely coupled, and it's all of their best interest to go and share the user identity. So that's likely.
cues.zh: 那网站、大型门户呢？嗯，我的意思是，你确实需要一个完整的身份生态系统。所以你需要大量用户。你需要一堆身份提供者和服务提供者，它们之间松散耦合，而共享用户身份符合它们所有人的最佳利益。所以这很有可能。

cues.en: But if you recall, Microsoft rolled out something called Passport that the Internet firmly rejected.
cues.zh: 但如果你还记得，微软推出过一项叫 Passport 的服务，结果被互联网坚决抵制了。

cues.en: And, you know, if you look at, well, why did that happen? Well, this is my speculation that it was expensive,
cues.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你看看，为什么会发生这种情况？嗯，这是我的推测，因为它很贵，

cues.en: didn't support LAMP, it was proprietary,
cues.zh: 不支持 LAMP，它是专有技术，

cues.en: it was really targeted for large sites only. Microsoft was at the center, and the only useful feature was single sign on.
cues.zh: 它实际上只针对大型网站。微软处于中心位置，唯一有用的功能就是单点登录。

cues.en: But, fortunately, we got a new era coming up.
cues.zh: 但幸运的是，我们正迎来一个新时代。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: I don't know why you guys are clapping about that.
cues.zh: 我不知道你们为什么为此鼓掌。

cues.en: So, we've got
cues.zh: 所以，我们有了

cues.en: Flickr, which got acquired by Yahoo, which I was excited about being an investor in them.
cues.zh: Flickr，它被 Yahoo 收购了，作为他们的投资者，我当时很兴奋。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: not only did they have a great site, but they had an API, so sites like Mapper could go and create sites using the tags about geographic locations and show you pictures from around The US, which is kind of US centric.
cues.zh: 他们不仅有一个很棒的网站，还提供了API，于是像Mapper这样的网站就能利用地理位置标签来建站，展示美国各地的照片，不过这有点以美国为中心。

cues.en: But being Canadian always have an issue with that. At sites like Crazy Dad, they could go and take all the circle square photos and create some pretty amazing artwork. So you have all these sites doing cool things on top of Flickr, but it isn't just
cues.zh: 但作为加拿大人，总会对此有意见。在Crazy Dad这样的网站上，他们可以拿所有圆形和方形的照片，创作出相当惊艳的艺术作品。所以有这么多网站都在Flickr之上做很酷的事，但这不仅仅

cues.en: in the consumer spaces that have Salesforce Tom, they created S Force, and you have all these companies creating products that run on top of all the data you got in S Force. And so this has been called Web two point o and O'Reilly has a conference, the next one coming up in October.
cues.zh: 是在消费级领域，Salesforce的Tom他们打造了S Force，于是有这么多公司在你S Force里的所有数据之上创建产品。所以这被称为Web 2.0，O'Reilly有一个大会，下一届就在十月。

cues.en: And it's sort of, I view it as the difference between DOS and Windows, where in DOS, could only run a single app at a time and in Windows, you could run multiple apps.
cues.zh: 这有点像，我把它看作DOS和Windows的区别，在DOS里一次只能运行一个应用，而在Windows里可以运行多个应用。

cues.en: And at run time, there's ability to be linking all the different components and all the different data. And in Windows, this was done in Calm, and in Web two point o, this is done with Web Services.
cues.zh: 而在运行时，能够把各个不同的组件和不同的数据链接起来。在Windows里，这是用COM做的，而在Web 2.0里，这是用Web Services做的。

cues.en: So you can have applications like this where S Force goes and grabs the maps from Google,
cues.zh: 所以你可以有像这样的应用，S Force去从Google抓取地图，

cues.en: and you can go and create a map showing you where all your customer locations are. Or say, try creating a profile site so you can put your Flickr photos in there and your delicious links in there and your Amazon wish list into it. But how does Tribe go and get Halsted's wish list from amazon.com?
cues.zh: 然后你可以创建一张地图，显示你所有客户的位置。或者比如，试着建一个个人主页，把你Flickr的照片放进去，把你的delicious链接放进去，把你的Amazon心愿单放进去。但Tribe要怎么从amazon.com拿到Halsted的心愿单呢？

cues.en: Well, Halsted had to give Tribe her amazon.com username and password. I mean, does anyone else see a problem with this? There's no granularity. They have full access to everything. So you need claims in order for Web Service Identity to really work. So I see that Web two point o is going to be one of the big drivers for Identity two point o.
cues.zh: Halsted 得把她在 amazon.com 的用户名和密码给 Tribe。我是说，还有别人觉得这有问题吗？完全没有粒度控制，他们能访问所有东西。所以要让 Web Service Identity 真正起作用，你需要声明机制。所以我认为 Web 2.0 将成为 Identity 2.0 的重要推动力之一。

cues.en: Well, Microsoft is back again around this, and you have Kim Cramer with his Identity web log and the laws of identity, which, by the way, is actually some pretty good work. And you have Infocard in the meta system, and is this Passport 2.0 or is it more like Identity 2.0?
cues.zh: 微软又回来搞这个了，还有 Kim Cramer 和他的 Identity 网志以及身份定律，顺便说一句，那其实是不错的工作。还有元系统里的 Infocard，这到底是 Passport 2.0 还是更像 Identity 2.0？

cues.en: And so, where are we technically on all this stuff? Well, we have XRI XDI, which is a par solution but nothing around web services. There's the Lightweight Identity, which I think is being presented later on today, as the name implies, it's lightweight and there's little security. So it solves part of the problem. There's OpenID, which is good for blogs,
cues.zh: 那么，这些东西在技术上进展到哪一步了？我们有 XRI XDI，这是个部分解决方案，但在 Web 服务方面没什么东西。还有 Lightweight Identity，我想今天晚些时候会有人介绍，顾名思义，它轻量，安全性也很少。所以它只解决了部分问题。还有 OpenID，对博客来说不错，

cues.en: but once again, little security.
cues.zh: 但同样，安全性很少。

cues.en: The Palcel guys rolled stuff, you know, talked about things yesterday, and it's open source. It's got stronger security, but there's lots of loose ends and still under development.
cues.zh: Palcel 那帮人搞了些东西，你知道，昨天谈了些事情，它是开源的。安全性更强，但有很多未了结的问题，还在开发中。

cues.en: You have SAML, which is logical progression for enterprises,
cues.zh: 还有 SAML，这是企业的合理演进，

cues.en: and there's some open source there as open SAML, but there's some real risk redistribution issues around there because in order to go and put that into a package, you gotta go and get a license from RSA.
cues.zh: 那里也有一些开源的，叫 Open SAML，但存在一些真正的再分发风险问题，因为要把它打包，你得去从 RSA 拿许可证。

cues.en: So is it really open source? In my view, not really. Is it simple? Well, lots of people don't think so. And is it suitable for millions of sites that only need simple data? Probably not. You have the WS Star stuff led by Microsoft and their friends, and so they got claims, but is it once again suitable for millions of sites, and does Infocard really mimic how photo ID works?
cues.zh: 那它真的开源吗？在我看来，并不算。它简单吗？很多人可不这么认为。它适合那些只需要简单数据的数百万网站吗？大概不适合。现在有微软及其伙伴主导的 WS-* 那套东西，他们确实有相关声明，但它是否又一次适合数百万网站？InfoCard 真的模拟了带照片身份证件的工作方式吗？

cues.en: And even more important, are Google and Yahoo going to support something that Microsoft drives?
cues.zh: 更重要的是，Google 和 Yahoo 会支持一个由微软推动的东西吗？

cues.en: So, over at SCIP, which obviously is pronounced Skip,
cues.zh: 那么，在 SCIP——显然读作 Skip——

cues.en: and stands for the Simple Extensible Identity Protocol, we have sort of two message formats. One, named value pairs that provides a very low barrier to entry for existing forms, and digitally signed XML for verified claims, and we've architected it to mimic how your
cues.zh: 它代表 Simple Extensible Identity Protocol，我们大概有两种消息格式。一种是名值对，为现有表单提供了极低的入门门槛；另一种是用于已验证声明的数字签名 XML。我们的架构设计让它模仿你的

cues.en: driver's license works.
cues.zh: 驾照如何运作。

cues.en: So what will win? I obviously would like Skip to win, but I don't know who's going to win.
cues.zh: 那什么会胜出？我显然希望 Skip 胜出，但我不知道谁会赢。

cues.en: But I do know that Identity two point is inevitable, so that I'll eventually be able to go and prove online that I'm Canadian, that I live here, I'm over 21, I went to UBC,
cues.zh: 但我确实知道 Identity 2.0 不可避免，所以最终我能在网上证明：我是加拿大人，我住在这里，我超过 21 岁，我上过 UBC，

cues.en: I work at Skip, and I am Star Alliance Gold.
cues.zh: 我在 Skip 工作，而且是星空联盟金卡会员。

cues.en: But if you want a world where your... It's your identity and not their identity, and the technology is open and not restricted,
cues.zh: 但如果你想要一个这样的世界：你的……这是你的身份，而不是他们的身份，技术是开放且不受限制的，

cues.en: and you don't know Dick about Identity 2.0,
cues.zh: 而且你对 Identity 2.0 一窍不通，

cues.en: join the conversation. You know, my blog I'm talking about this stuff, and together we can go and create an Identity two point architecture that works for all of us. Thank you.
cues.zh: 那就加入讨论吧。你知道，我在博客里就在聊这些，我们可以一起打造一个适合所有人的 Identity 2.0 架构。谢谢。
